question: Refer to the exhibit. What happens to the broadcast traffic when it reaches aggregation switches?
context: Topology: Agg-1 and Agg-2 connected via a peer link (Eth2/4, Eth2/5). Agg-1 (Port channel55/vPC-1) and Agg-2 (Port channel56/vPC-2) each connect down to Access-1 and Access-2 (Eth2/1, Eth2/2), which host Vlan20 and Vlan10 devices. Broadcast flooding is shown originating from Access-1/Vlan20 hosts.
options: Agg-2 switch receives broadcast packets and stops forwarding to the peer link on Agg-1 switch.
Agg-1 prevents broadcast packets received on the vPC peer link from exiting the switch on ports Eth2/4 and Eth2/5.
Agg-1 and Agg-2 switches receive broadcast packets and does not forward them to the peer link or the port channel.
Only Agg-1 switch receives broadcast packets and does not forward to the peer link on Agg-2 switch.
